questions.q: Can you ___ the children while I am out?
questions.why: 'Look after' means to take care of someone.

questions.q: I don't know this word; let me ___ it ___ in the dictionary.
questions.why: 'Look up' means to find information in a reference source.

questions.q: I have been ___ my keys all morning.
questions.why: 'Look for' means to try to find something.

questions.q: It was hard, but he never ___ trying.
questions.why: 'Give up' means to stop doing something, especially trying.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'Smoking is bad for you, so you should give ___ it.'
questions.why: 'Give up' means to quit a habit.

questions.q: They had to ___ the wedding because she got sick.
questions.why: 'Put off' means to postpone something to a later time.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'Don't ___ off until tomorrow what you can do today.'
questions.why: 'Put off' means to delay or postpone.

questions.q: The plane will ___ in ten minutes.
questions.why: 'Take off' means to leave the ground and begin to fly.

questions.q: Please ___ your shoes ___ before entering.
questions.why: 'Take off' also means to remove clothing or shoes.

questions.q: They offered her the job, but she ___ it ___.
questions.why: 'Turn down' means to refuse or reject an offer.

questions.q: Could you ___ the music? It is too loud.
questions.why: 'Turn down' also means to lower the volume or level.

questions.q: We have ___ ___ milk, so I need to buy some.
questions.why: 'Run out of' means to have no more of a supply.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'The car stopped because it ran ___ ___ petrol.'
questions.why: 'Run out of' means to use up all of something.

questions.q: How do you ___ ___ your new colleagues?
questions.why: 'Get on with' means to have a good relationship with someone.

questions.q: I am really ___ ___ the holidays next week.
questions.why: 'Look forward to' means to feel excited about a future event; it takes a noun or -ing.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'I look forward ___ hearing from you soon.'
questions.why: 'Look forward to' is always followed by 'to' plus a noun or -ing form.

questions.q: My car ___ on the motorway and I had to call for help.
questions.why: 'Break down' means to stop working (for machines or vehicles).

questions.q: Despite the rain, the team decided to ___ ___ the match.
questions.why: 'Carry on' means to continue doing something.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'You are doing well, so please carry ___.'
questions.why: 'Carry on' means to continue.

questions.q: Grandma will ___ the baby while we are at work.
questions.why: 'Look after' means to take care of someone.

questions.q: The negotiations ___ ___ when the two sides disagreed.
questions.why: 'Break down' can also mean to fail or collapse, as with talks.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'I admire her; I really look ___ ___ her.'
questions.why: 'Look up to' means to admire or respect someone.

questions.q: He decided to ___ ___ chocolate for a month.
questions.why: 'Give up' means to stop having or doing something.

questions.q: We should not ___ ___ the decision any longer.
questions.why: 'Put off' means to delay or postpone.

questions.q: She ___ ___ his offer of help politely.
questions.why: 'Turn down' means to refuse politely.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'We are running ___ ___ time, so hurry up.'
questions.why: 'Run out of' means to have almost none of something left.

questions.q: I hope you ___ ___ your new flatmate.
questions.why: 'Get on with' means to have a friendly relationship with someone.

questions.q: The students ___ ___ working even after the bell rang.
questions.why: 'Carry on' means to keep doing something.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'My old washing machine broke ___ again.'
questions.why: 'Break down' means to stop functioning.

questions.q: Remember to ___ the new word ___ if you don't understand it.
questions.why: 'Look up' means to search for information in a dictionary or online.

questions.q: The plane ___ on time despite the storm.
questions.why: 'Take off' = leave the ground (plane).

questions.q: I'll ___ the kids from school today.
questions.why: 'Pick up' = collect someone.

questions.q: We had to ___ the meeting until Friday.
questions.why: 'Put off' = postpone.

questions.q: She ___ the whole story — none of it was true.
questions.why: 'Make up' = invent (a story, an excuse).

questions.q: Never ___ ! You're almost at the finish line.
questions.why: 'Give up' = stop trying.
